bottom: Ossoff is the top raising Senate candidate in the country and leads Republican Mike Collins in public polling. He raised $33 million from July through September 2026 and had $26 million in cash, against Collins's $2.7 million and just over $1.1 million, per the Georgia Recorder on October 15, 2026, https://georgiarecorder.com/2026/10/15/ossoff-reports-raising-another-33-million-for-homestretch-of-u-s-senate-reelection-bid/. An AJC and UGA poll fielded October 7 to 15 had Ossoff 48 and Collins 40, per Fox 5 Atlanta, https://www.fox5atlanta.com/news/ajc-poll-gives-ossoff-8-point-lead-over-collins.
Interests that combine money and a decision:
**Small donors.** About 760,000 third quarter donations, nearly 97 percent under $100. They want lower costs, which he frames as repealing tariffs, ending the Iran war and reversing Medicaid cuts.
**Party and leadership.** Senate Majority PAC reserved $20 million for him in May, he has passed more than $3.6 million to other Democrats, and SMP linked groups are spending against Collins.

D.t: Jon Ossoff leads by 10.2 in the forecast and wins 98% of simulations. The cushion is about 475,268 votes; a one point swing is about 23,343 voters changing sides.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between D +4.4 and D +16.0. Only an unusual polling error changes the winner.
The polls page average is D +9.7. Your best recent poll is Big Data Poll (R) at D +12.4; your worst is Quantus Insights at D +5.8. 9 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Fulton, a projected net 287,179 votes; DeKalb, a projected net 261,648 votes; Gwinnett, a projected net 118,602 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Houston, R +0.1, 1.5% of the vote; Fayette, D +8.7, 1.4% of the vote; Lowndes, R +7.5, 0.9% of the vote; Spalding, R +6.4, 0.6% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Jon Ossoff runs furthest behind in Walton, Hall, Bartow. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 69% of voters, 55 to 44, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.47 points; White voters, 62% of voters, 41 to 57, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.12 points; Voters without a degree, 60% of voters, 51 to 48, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.00 points.
The forecast's worst groups for Jon Ossoff: Immigration voters 19 to 80, Small counties 32 to 67, White voters 41 to 57. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$42.6M cash against $1.2M. Spend it early on persuasion television in the battleground counties and keep a reserve for the last week.
